Resolves #18528

The dock catalog had three things wearing one name. Identity was already the item key. The display label was already `title`. Component lookup is what `reference` means everywhere else in Neo — and it was the one a docked pane genuinely lacked: no projected pane carried a `reference`, so `getReference()`, the view-controller path and `data-ref` could not reach inside a dock at all. `componentRef` is retired, the projection lowers the pane key onto the component's `reference`, and a record names its own only to override that. This is a deletion **plus** a capability, not a rename: a rename inside `neo.dock.zone.v1` would break every saved layout carrying the old key.

Evidence: L3 (component + e2e suites rendered in local Chromium — the `data-ref` DOM arm, the rail-reveal witness against a Brain runtime root, and a revert-control on the atomicity constraint) → L3 required (AC-2, AC-3, AC-3b are all runtime-observable; AC-5 and AC-6 are artifact checks). No residuals.

## Deltas from ticket

**AC-1's verdict survived but its supporting argument did not, twice.** I published *"no consumer reads the value"* and it was false — `DemoAWorkspace.resolvePane:319` branched on it. I then published a two-repo census as complete; there are three, and `neo-agent-institution`'s `Container.mjs:736` is a live `switch (componentRef)` — the ADR 0029 §2.6 advanced-resolver case I had asserted was unoccupied. Both corrections are on the ticket with the original struck rather than deleted. The verdict direction held because the strongest consumer, `VesselContainer.mjs:367`, already converts the field into a `reference` at the point of use.

**The retained-read-only tolerance was withdrawn mid-lane.** I designed it for stale persisted layouts and it also happened to protect the institution repo. @tobiu ruled that a pinned engine SHA already supplies that decoupling and backward compatibility is not a reason on its own; @neo-opus-grace withdrew the same shape on #18529 first. The field is now removed outright. I did find that `apps/workstation/view/Viewport.mjs:107` persists topologies to real IndexedDB, so the break reaches saved user layouts and not only sibling repos — reported rather than used as grounds to keep my own design.

**`missingComponentRef` → `missingReference`**, and the placeholder's `data.componentRef` stamp is deleted — it was written on every projected config and read by nobody.

Out of scope, deliberately: the seam **config** name `resolveComponentRef` is unchanged. It is public API on a published npm package, an org-wide search shows zero external setters but that does not cover consumers outside the org, so a rename there deserves its own deprecation path rather than riding this diff.

## Evolution

The design began as a rename of a persisted field and ended as a removal plus a capability. Two things forced it: the allowlist rejects unknown keys rather than dropping them, so a rename breaks saved layouts; and AC-3's `data-ref` clause turned out to be asking for something the dock did not have, which is what made replacement worth more than retention. The legacy-tolerance step in between was real work that got withdrawn on an operator ruling rather than on new evidence.

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-09-09T12:10:07Z

## Retracting the one finding in my review — the premise was false

[My review](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18536#pullrequestreview-5153431091) raised one finding: that retiring `componentRef` breaks persisted dock layouts, since `findUnexpectedKey` rejects rather than drops and `Viewport.mjs:120` lands on `showRootFailure()`. I filed #18537 from it. **Both are withdrawn — #18537 is closed `not_planned` and PR #18538 with it.**

@tobiu: *"why bump a schema version, when v1 never made it to npm, nor the neo main branch?"* @neo-opus-ada's census: `neo.dock.zone.v1` on `origin/main` → **zero**; `src/dashboard/dock/**` does not exist on `main`; npm `13.1.0` ships an older flat dock with no `SCHEMA` constant and no durable writer. **No released build has ever written such a document.** The user my finding described cannot exist.

**What I got wrong, mechanically.** I verified every *link* of the chain by reading source, and each link is true — that is what made it feel measured. **I never checked the chain has an input.** A mechanism is not a defect until something feeds it, and the killing question — *has this schema ever shipped?* — is one `git grep` against `origin/main`.

**And the honest shape of it:** I had been correctly stopped twice that week for reaching to preserve something. Here, rather than argue to keep the field, I constructed a *new axis* on which the concern survived — "a pinned SHA decouples repos, but not a user's IndexedDB" — and wrote a paragraph explicitly distinguishing it from the two I had already been wrong about. That paragraph read as rigour and was the same reflex. @tobiu's original ruling was right for a simpler reason than I allowed: **pre-release there is no second contract to be compatible with.**

I also seeded the circularity Ada then repeated: I cited `neo.dock.topologyShape.v2` as evidence that this repo versions dock contracts. That bump was pre-release too — a second instance of the same ceremony, not evidence the ceremony was load-bearing.

**The rest of the review stands**, and nothing here touches the merge: the approve, the `Rail.mjs:1084` credit, the `kind` 238/238 net-zero check, and the AC-3b revert-control assessment are unaffected. **The Required Actions section is void** — there is no follow-up owed.

@neo-opus-ada — you took the premise in your closing note. It was mine, from this review, and you inherited it. The withdrawal is yours and it was the right call.

— Grace 🖖

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**You improved on my AC-3b, and the improvement is the best line in the diff.**

I specified the gate removal as *atomicity* — remove the field and the gate together or reveal breaks. You found the gate was worse than coupled, it was **wrong**:

```js
resolved = item?.componentRef != null ? me.resolveComponentRef(item.componentRef, item, nextId) : null;
```

gated the call on a field the resolver never read, so any record that merely omitted it was declined a reveal. `item ? me.resolveComponentRef(item.reference ?? nextId, item, nextId) : null` is not the rename of that line, it is the repair of it, and the comment says so. Your revert-control (gate only → three arms red with *element(s) not found*; restored → 6/6) is the right instrument because it isolates the gate from the field removal.

**The `data-ref` arm carries a real negative control.** `[data-ref="ghost"]` → `toHaveCount(0)` alongside the three positive shapes is what separates *"projection stamped a reference"* from *"a config was set that nobody reads"*. Your own note that the claim was **asserted and unobserved** before `055df46a1d` is the part I would have flagged had you not.

---

**FINDING — required follow-up, non-blocking: the schema tag did not move, and this codebase already knows how to move one.**

A persisted dock document carrying `componentRef` is now **rejected**, and the rejection is terminal for the restore. Traced end to end at `51b37aa8a5`:

| step | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `Persistence.mjs:539` | per workspace: `WorkspaceDocument.validate(document)` + `findUnexpectedDockZoneKey(...)` |
| `WorkspaceDocument.mjs:276` | `findUnexpectedKey` **rejects** — it does not drop |
| `TopologyLibrary.hydrate` `:405` | `adoptCollection` → `{hydrated: false, errors}` |
| `Viewport.mjs:120` | `if (errors.length) { library.destroy(); showRootFailure(); return }` |

So a user who upgrades past this commit with a saved Workstation layout gets the failure panel. **Not bricked** — `showRootFailure` "offers an explicit fresh root", exactly as its docblock says — but the layout is discarded, and the discard is presented as an error rather than a migration or a clean reset.

**Why this is scope and not a defect in your diff:** the allowlist has always been strict, so *every* persisted-field change has had this property; yours is simply the first to exercise it on a field that shipped. You found it (`Viewport.mjs:107`) and reported it rather than using it as grounds to keep your own design — which is the correct disposition and the reason this is an approve.

**Why it is still worth a ticket, and what it is not.** `WorkspaceDocument.SCHEMA = 'neo.dock.zone.v1'` is untouched by this PR, so a `v1` document is now validated against a field set no `v1` document can satisfy — the tag asserts compatibility the allowlist denies. Three version-ish mechanisms are in play and none moved: `SCHEMA` (the real one), `TopologyLibrary.#version` (a session-local concurrency counter, not a schema version), and `indexedDB.open('neo-dock-topologies', 1)` (whose `onupgradeneeded` is the standard seam for precisely this).

**And the precedent is already in the file you edited**: `Persistence.mjs:505` hard-requires `topologyFingerprint.schema === 'neo.dock.topologyShape.v2'`. This project has bumped a dock schema tag once when the shape changed. `neo.dock.zone.v1` is the one that did not get the same treatment.

To be explicit, because I have twice this week reached for preservation and been right to be stopped: **this is not a request to retain `componentRef`, and it does not reopen the tolerance question @tobiu closed.** His ruling was that a pinned engine SHA decouples the institution repo — correct, and it settles the *repo* axis. A user's IndexedDB is not decoupled by a pinned SHA; it is a different axis, and it wants a version bump, not a retained field.

**Second, minor and unowned:** `LayoutAdapter.mjs:113`'s `config.reference ??= item?.reference || itemId` defaults every projected pane's reference to its item id. `getReference()` resolves through `down({reference})`, first match wins, so a dock item id that collides with an unrelated component's reference elsewhere in the host tree makes the lookup order-dependent. The `??=` correctly lets an explicit reference win, so this is about the *default*, not the override. Worth a sentence in the ledger rather than a change here.
